Rules and teacher notes

Attacks disrupt relations: Choosing to attack another country, or besieging/capturing its owned land, breaks the alliance and cancels joint research between the two countries. Both lose the extra joint progress and 25% refund; funded independent research can still progress normally if they retain a safe settlement. Pending trade and knowledge offers are cancelled, and trade escrow is returned exactly once. No new trade, knowledge sharing or joint research between those countries is allowed through the next round. One full round without another attack restores exchanges at the following planning phase; another attack restarts that wait. Forming an alliance alone does not shorten it. Completed trades, previously learned discoveries, research progress and earned objectives remain. Neutral land claims and simply moving/holding do not disrupt relations. Other partners remain available.

Objectives and victory: All nine department objectives are always available. No selection or lock-in. Complete any three across at least two departments; Economy + R&D offers peaceful victory. Awards are checked only after the full round, are permanent, and countries finishing together share victory. Streaks reset on missed requirements. See each department’s cards for current progress and the teacher guide for exact trade/action safeguards. Teachers may continue after a victory.

Four stages: plan orders → agree alliances and choose countries to attack → resolve combat and choose retreats → review results. Only the teacher advances. This local prototype exposes all countries to its host; it does not yet provide private student logins.

Regiments: 100 health when recruited. Spears beat cavalry; cavalry beat archers; archers beat spears. Artillery is neutral against all unit types, with normal damage in both directions. It deals double damage to settlement defenses. Advantage ×1.5, disadvantage ×0.75. Base damage is 30% of the regiment’s current health, modified by type, travel fatigue, allies and pursuit. Damage is simultaneous. Equipment tiers add 10% attack each while preserving type advantages. Fully supplied troops on their own happy territory gain up to 5% morale attack. Hospital treatment is the only recovery ability; soldiers are not mixed individually.

Movement: 2 territories per turn, up to 4 with research. Empty foreign land can be crossed. Hostile troops block a route through their location. Meeting during travel stops movement; opposing armies crossing the same edge meet in the lower-numbered territory. Rough territory crossed reduces attack by 15%, capped at 30%.

Country targets: choose one opponent per contested territory or hold. Each regiment attacks once; its country’s combined damage budget is shared among its opponent’s regiments in proportion to health. Several opponents add their damage before it is applied. Mutually agreed allies attacking the same opponent gain ×1.5 damage, except when that opponent attacks them back. Attacking an ally breaks that alliance after the simultaneous exchange.

Retreat: a damaged country with fewer surviving troops than the strongest force at the site must retreat one adjacent territory. Ties hold. No safe escape means surrender. Retreat preserves damage. During the next cycle, a retreat-marked regiment moving away takes ×2 damage if a previous attacker catches it again. The mark then expires.

Capture: only a capture order claims land. After retreats, a sole country with ready capture-order regiments besieges the territory. Ownership changes only when its defenses reach zero. Shared settlement captures require unanimous agreement about the new owner. Other disputed territory keeps its owner. Each controlled territory produces food and wood from its full biome mixture, scaled modestly by land area. Metal comes from marked deposits. Coastal fishing adds 2 food. Production enters Treasury after the full round. Recruitment uses distinct costs shown in Military: spears need more metal, archers more wood, cavalry more food and equipment, and artillery the most metal. Six living regiments maximum per country. Cavalry and artillery require R&D unlocks.

Food and happiness: Each territory needs 1–3 food based on land area, rising with settlement level to a maximum of 5. During Retreat & feed, Economy assigns Treasury food and confirms for each country with land. Full rations give +10 happiness; missing food costs up to 30 points, proportional to the shortfall. Happiness ranges from 0 to 100 and multiplies production from 0.5 to 1.5. Capturing land resets happiness to 0 after feeding; the new owner begins feeding it next retreat phase. New games start with 120 Treasury food; older saves keep their existing stocks.

Military meals: After budget deliveries, each surviving regiment—including trainees—uses 1 Military food automatically. A shortage raises damage taken next round by up to 50%, proportional to missing food. The next meal recalculates the penalty. No food is taken from Treasury automatically. Recruitment food costs vary by unit type. Production collected this round cannot pay for this round’s civilian meal or military delivery.

Economy: Valid allocations save as you type. Treasury reserves unassigned resources; assigned funds are held for delivery after the full round. Military and Research can spend only their delivered balances in the next planning round. New production arrives in Treasury and must be allocated in a later round. Pending allocations can be revised during planning; they do not repeat automatically.

Recruitment and training: Recruit at a controlled village, town or city without hostile troops. Existing imported settlements are used; generated maps use their existing capitals. New recruits become ready next round. While training they cannot move or capture, and only defend against their country’s selected attacker, at half attack strength. They still take normal damage and can be forced to retreat. Existing starting units are ready immediately.

Settlements and defenses: Economy builds from Treasury during planning. Click a territory on the map. Build in order: Village → Small Town → Town → City → Great City. Their production bonuses are +25%, +50%, +75%, +100%, +150%, multiplied by happiness. Food need is the greater of the original land need or settlement level, capped at 5. Settlement defense health is 40 / 70 / 110 / 160 / 220. Palisade → Stone Walls → Citadel adds 60 / 140 / 240 health. Small towns/palisades require Construction; towns/stone walls require Masonry; cities require Urban Planning; great cities/citadels require Architecture. Existing settlements remain usable. One construction or repair per territory per round, shared with facility installation; no building beside hostile troops. Upgrades require undamaged defenses. Repairs restore up to 60 health for one money and one wood per 3 health, rounded up. These passive defenses prevent capture; they do not fire on troops. After retreats, each ready regiment ordered to capture deals 30% of its health as siege damage (artillery 60%), reduced by travel fatigue. Damage persists. Capturing removes all fortifications, lowers the settlement by two levels (minimum open land), leaves defenses at zero, and resets happiness to zero.

Shared captures: Several countries can combine siege damage when every remaining country has ready capture-order troops, the old owner is gone, and they did not attack one another this round. If a settlement’s defenses reach zero, each participating country must submit an ownership decision during resolution. All must choose the same participating country. The agreed owner receives the settlement with the normal two-level loss, destroyed fortifications and zero happiness. If votes differ or anyone chooses No agreement, the entire settlement is destroyed, the territory becomes unclaimed, and every occupying regiment withdraws one adjacent territory with its remaining health. Its arrival route is preferred, then another safe neighbor; no safe neighbor means surrender. Withdrawals use the same occupation snapshot and show movement arrows. Troops meeting after withdrawal can face a new conflict next round. Missing votes block resolution; they never count as rejection. Changing an ordinary retreat clears the ownership votes because the occupation may change. Open land keeps the previous sole-country capture rule.

R&D projects: One active national project. Choose a discovery with completed prerequisites, then pay one installment from delivered Research resources each planning round. Unfunded progress pauses and remains saved. Discoveries take 2–4 funded progress; results arrive after the full round. A safe controlled settlement is required; losing all safe settlements wastes that round’s funded work. Copper → Bronze → Iron → Steel improves spear equipment; Simple Bow → Recurved Bow → Longbow improves archers; Riding → Saddles → Stirrups unlocks/improves cavalry. Artillery has one unlock and no combat upgrade; Manufacturing reduces its recruitment cost 20%. Movement and production improvements have their own branches. Existing units pay Military resources to re-equip at a safe settlement and must rest for that round.

Specialties and graphs: Each country has Agriculture, Industry or Metallurgy as its specialty: +25% food, wood or metal respectively, and 25% lower installment costs in that research branch. Geography and deposits remain important; a bonus cannot create a missing deposit. Production discoveries multiply base yields alongside happiness and settlement levels. R&D’s graph shows actual production gained each round, separately from spending and trade.

City facilities: Only the R&D role view shows individual facilities in controlled settlements; this is not secure privacy on a shared host. Settlement level provides 1–5 slots. R&D installs unlocked facilities using delivered Research funds. Each settlement gets one paid active ability per round. Hospital: +20 health to one ready, damaged regiment that rests, avoids combat and receives full military food. Workshop: consume wood/metal to deliver 12 military metal next round. Academy: after funding research, buy +1 research progress, at most one academy boost nationally per round. Granary: transfer 6 Research food to Treasury, costing 2 money. Civic Hall: pay for +10 local happiness. Facility effects stop if the city is lost or occupied by hostile troops. Capture removes facilities beyond the reduced settlement’s slot limit; destruction removes them all.

Knowledge and cooperation: Offer a completed discovery for free; the recipient must accept and meet its prerequisites. A captured city of level 4 or 5 can grant one of its former owner’s discoveries, chosen by R&D. The owner keeps its knowledge. Each city provides archives only once to each capturing country; disagreement destruction grants none. For joint research, both countries select the same project and accept a partnership before either funds it. If both fund and retain safe settlements, each receives an extra progress point and a 25% refund of its installment (rounded down per resource). Renew the partnership each round. No funding from one partner means no joint bonus or refund.

Economic trade: Offer unreserved Treasury resources for an agreed bundle of money, food, wood or metal. The offered goods enter escrow immediately; only the recipient can accept and pay the requested amount. Declining, cancelling or expiry at round-end returns escrow exactly. Accepted resources enter Treasury; department delivery delays still apply. Gifts are allowed, self-trades and negative or fractional offers are not. No preset exchange rate: students negotiate based on their countries’ needs and production.

Geography and biome import adapted from Azgaar (MIT). Geometry uses D3 Delaunay. Rule balance is ready for classroom playtesting, not a historical prediction.
